title: Domain I: Regulatory & Compliance - CPPB Domain I: Regulatory & Compliance - Protection of Trade Secrets
subject: CPPB Domain I: Regulatory & Compliance

questions.q: For a vendor's information to be legally protected from public disclosure as a 'Trade Secret,' the information must generally possess independent economic value from not being known AND:
options: Be copyrighted with the US Copyright Office.
Be the subject of efforts that are reasonable under the circumstances to maintain its secrecy.
Relate solely to computer software code.
questions.explain: Under the Uniform Trade Secrets Act (UTSA), a trade secret must derive independent economic value from its secrecy and the owner must make reasonable efforts to maintain that secrecy.
questions.subject: CPPB Domain I: Regulatory & Compliance

questions.q: A vendor submits a proposal and stamps every single page, including the cover page and table of contents, as 'CONFIDENTIAL - TRADE SECRET.' How should a public procurement officer legally view this?
options: The entire document must be shielded from the public permanently.
Blanket confidentiality claims are generally invalid; only specific data meeting the legal definition of a trade secret is exempt from disclosure.
The proposal must be rejected immediately as non-responsive.
The buyer must sue the vendor for making a false claim.
questions.explain: Vendors often over-designate their materials as confidential. Blanket designations are rarely legally binding. The burden remains on identifying specific information (like formulas or client lists) that truly meets the statutory definition of a trade secret.
questions.subject: CPPB Domain I: Regulatory & Compliance

questions.q: Which of the following elements of a vendor's successful bid is almost NEVER legally protected as a trade secret or confidential information?
options: The total bottom-line price or contract amount offered to the public agency.
Detailed blueprints of a highly secure banking vault.
questions.explain: How public money is spent is the cornerstone of public records law. Therefore, the final pricing, bottom-line contract cost, and public funds exchanged are almost universally forbidden from being claimed as confidential trade secrets.
questions.subject: CPPB Domain I: Regulatory & Compliance

questions.q: If a government employee knowingly and willfully releases a vendor's highly guarded, clearly marked, and legally validated trade secret to a competitor to sabotage the vendor, this employee has most likely committed:
options: A breach of the Perfect Tender Rule
questions.explain: Misappropriation occurs when a trade secret is acquired, disclosed, or used by someone who knows or has reason to know that the secret was acquired by improper means.
